Dopina / pavilion manufacturers and sellers

From enquiry
to finished
pavilion.

Sales, configuration, pricing, production, and settlements. Connected around a single order.

Dopina is a system developed by ISIKO combining customer service and company operations. For pavilion manufacturers and sellers, we tailor the scope based on the process we designed and are developing for a pavilion manufacturer.

Dopina for manufacturers

One order.
The full picture.

A customer asks about a 6 × 3 m commercial pavilion. Then they change the equipment, request a new variant, and agree on a delivery date. The sales rep needs an up-to-date quote. Production — an approved scope. The warehouse — information about materials. Accounting — documents and payments.

We show this journey below. This is how Dopina works. STAGO — a manufacturer of modular pavilions — uses the system. Companies, people, and amounts are fictional. The implementation covers the scope agreed for your company — from the first enquiry to handover.

01 / The customer and their enquiry

The conversation has
a next step.

The enquiry is assigned an owner, a status, and a date for the next contact. Customer requirements, notes, prepared quotes, and a link to fulfilment stay with the enquiry.

The sales rep sees whom to follow up with, what is missing for the quote, and what stage the conversation is at. Filters allow focusing on one's own cases, a specific status, or a deadline. Changing the lead person does not have to mean reconstructing agreed details from email inboxes and phone calls.

In our example, the starting point is a commercial pavilion. The description of needs becomes the basis for configuration. Subsequent agreed details stay attached to the same case — even if the customer returns after several weeks.

02 / Specification and quote

Dimensions and equipment
are costed in the quote.

Length, width, height, structure, and equipment go into the configurator. Line items have a quantity, unit, variant, and calculation rule. It is clear what makes up the price.

Changing the scope without recalculating from scratch

The configurator supports catalog, mandatory, and optional items. Quantities can derive from dimensions or be entered manually. The quote takes into account materials, labor, transport, margin, and VAT. A fixed price mode is also available.

When the customer changes the equipment, the sales rep updates the relevant line items. Notes on an element or category organize the details that should go into the quote.

Templates and pricing responsibility

A recurring set can be based on a template. The quote has its own number, validity period, notes, and attachments. Access and required approvals are tailored to the responsibilities of the sales rep and the person approving the quote.

AI support in the configurator helps complete and verify the quote. The sales rep verifies line items and amounts before the next step. A pavilion floor plan can be attached to the case as a document.

03 / Agreement with the customer

The customer sees
the agreed scope.

The online quote and PDF document lead to a specific price calculation. The customer can review the scope and provide feedback. Access to the quote and its acceptance may require confirmation via SMS code.

This is a key moment in the process: the proposal, quote version, and customer confirmation should relate to the same agreed details. The implementation includes agreeing on approval methods, responsibilities, and documents used by your company.

In our example, after specifying the equipment in detail, the sales rep prepares the quote, and the accepted scope becomes the basis for further fulfilment.

04 / From agreed details to execution

Production works
on the same order.

The project connects the customer, quote number, dimensions, status, and planned date. The team sees what is in preparation, what is being built, and what is nearly ready for handover.

On the list, you can compare fulfilment progress and deadlines. The project card gathers details needed to perform the work. A status change may require additional information, such as assigning a serial number before entering a specific stage.

The fulfilment deadline and transport are related, yet separate agreed details. Their visibility helps coordinate the shop floor, office, and handover preparation. We adapt the process depending on whether you manufacture from scratch, assemble modules, or sell finished pavilions.

You know what is available.
And where it went.

05 / Materials and identification

Material records, available quantities, allocated resources, and minimum stock levels help prepare the work. Issues, returns, and receipts create its warehouse context.

Warehouse connected with fulfilment

Material can be issued to an order, and any unused portion can be returned. The movement history allows tracking changes. Low stock levels are visible in the system and can feed the view of the person responsible for procurement.

The featured STAGO warehouse workflow uses Subiekt nexo. The warehouse variant requires agreeing on integration with Subiekt nexo PRO and the data bridge: records, stock levels, issues, and documents. For an implementation without ERP, we start with sales, quotes, and fulfilment; a standalone warehouse is a separate scope to prepare and accept.

The pavilion has its own number

Serial numbers are generated in batches and assigned to projects. Used and available numbers are visible. This gives document preparation and project identification a common point of reference.

We separately determine material batch tracking and supply traceability requirements. We do not assume that the pavilion serial number solves all warehouse needs.

Working time is recorded
against the pavilion.

06 / Daily shop floor operations

The employee selects the fulfilment project, enters the time, and can describe what they did. They view their own workday on their phone without navigating a complex office dashboard.

The system distinguishes between attendance and work assigned to a specific pavilion or frame. Saved entries are shown for the relevant workday. This provides data for further review and analysis of the labour required for each project.

During implementation, we agree on how time is reported, who is responsible for corrections, the devices used on the shop floor, and the connection to existing employee records. Time tracking and integration with HR and payroll software are separate implementation scopes.

Agreed work.
Clear payment records.

07 / Documents and payments

The order links the customer, quote, documents, and payments. You can see how much has been paid, what amount remains, and which cases need attention.

The payment status is based on documents and payments. The person handling the order can open its details from the list. Linking amounts to documents reduces the need to compare several separate summaries.

Attachments, confirmations, and the operation history are part of the workflow. We agree where documents are created, who approves their content, and how data is passed to the accounting software in use. Access to financial information depends on the person's role in the company.

Ready means
checked.

08 / Readiness and handover

The quality checklist guides the employee through the pavilion's inspection points. Answers, notes, and photos help document its condition before handover.

Each section shows the inspection progress. A nonconformity may require clarification, and completing the checklist has its own confirmation step. The questions are tailored to what the company actually manufactures.

Handover documents and transport details complete the operational part. Implementation includes agreeing when an order can be considered ready, who is responsible for acceptance, and what information should reach the customer.

Agreed details stay recorded.
The team knows what comes next.

09 / Communication and a shared overview

Conversation history and summaries help recover the customer's context. The dashboard brings together deadlines, reminders, and sales, production, and financial matters.

Conversations can be linked to the customer's case. When the channel is integrated, AI-assisted transcripts and summaries are available. Their role is to support the person handling the contact. The scope of recording, access, and use of the content must be agreed within the company.

Users can arrange their own dashboard, pin important cases, and choose the widgets they need. Sales staff, production, and management use connected information while viewing what they need for their work.

At the start of the day

What is approaching its deadline? Who needs a follow-up? Which material is missing? Which order has already been settled? The dashboard provides a starting point for these matters and lets you open the details.

The case has context.
The company keeps moving.

Options for extending Dopina

We select further integrations to suit the team's work. First, we agree which problem they should solve, then we prepare a specific workflow and carry out acceptance checks.

Shared inbox and WhatsApp

Email, SMS, and WhatsApp can be handled together with the customer's case, the history of agreed details, and the responsible person. A shared inbox brings channels together around the case. Enabling a channel includes connecting the account, setting permissions, and checking both sending and receiving.

AI in day-to-day work

Contact history and agreed details can help assess the situation: what is missing, where the risks lie, and which contact is worth making next. The sales rep receives a suggestion with its reasoning alongside the customer's case.

When preparing a quote, the model can find a similar earlier quote and suggest line items based on dimensions and specifications. The system calculates amounts using rates and rules. An authorised person checks the scope before approving the quote.

We define the data available to the model, the approval rules, and how the output is assessed. Explore our approach to implementing AI.

Notes, tasks, and deadlines

A note stays with the case, a task gets an owner and a deadline, and a reminder helps you return to the next step. If the process requires it, we can extend the scope to include a Gantt view, dependencies, and planned and actual task values. We agree on the calculation and planning methods before implementation.

A website connected to the company

A website form can create a case in Dopina. Selected information about the offering or completed projects can flow back to the website. We agree on the data source, update frequency, and error notifications so the team knows what has been published.

Scope for implementation

Pavilion complete?
Show it in your portfolio.

Final photos and a description can be used in the company's portfolio. We design a workflow in which the person in charge selects the materials, prepares the description, and submits them for approval before publication on the website. You can return to the original order, edit the content, and withdraw the publication.

Inspection photos remain part of the work documentation. Only a selected, approved set goes into the portfolio. This workflow connects production with marketing without collecting the materials again.

Your company, your scope

We start with the process.
We implement in stages.

A solution for a manufacturer with its own production facility may have a different scope from a system for a seller of ready-made modules. First, we establish where information gets lost and which part is worth connecting first.

What we agree before building

  • Pavilion types, equipment options, and pricing rules.
  • Sales, approval, fulfilment, and handover stages.
  • Roles, responsibilities, and data access.
  • The current ERP, documents, master records, and data to migrate.
  • Shop floor, warehouse, transport, and financial settlement requirements.

How we move into day-to-day use

We choose the first coherent workflow, prepare it with the team, and check it against agreed examples. We add further modules with acceptance criteria. We agree on training, support, data backups, and further development.

We prepare the implementation quote after assessing the scope. We describe the costs of external services, integrations, and maintenance separately. We do not require every working tool to be replaced.

Before the first conversation

Worth clarifying
at the start.

Does the solution make sense for a company that only sells pavilions?

Yes. The scope can focus on enquiries, configuration, quotes, supplier orders, transport, and settlement. We include shop floor modules when they match the company's actual work.

Can we keep our current ERP?

We start by checking the available integrations and responsibility for data. We establish which system manages master records, prices, stock levels, and documents. Only then do we design the exchange of information.

Does the configurator include 3D pavilion design?

The configurator shown is used for quotes: dimensions, items, variants, and calculation rules. Floor plans can be attached to the enquiry. A spatial editor would be a separate scope requiring design and quotation.

Do all modules need to be implemented at the same time?

No. We can start with a single workflow, for example enquiry → quote → handover to fulfilment. However, stages should use consistent data so that subsequent implementation does not require starting from scratch.

What should be prepared for the first conversation?

A sample order, description of equipment changes, current quote, and a list of tools used. To start with, an example without customer data and purchase prices is sufficient. Together, we will go from enquiry to acceptance.
